decisive_items: subjective fevers, rhinorrhea, a dry cough, and sinus congestion
ST-segment elevations with PR-segment depression in leads II, III, and aVF
Initial serum troponin I level: 6.18 ng/mL
response.rationale: The patient's symptoms of fever and cough, along with the elevated troponin level, could suggest myocarditis, although the normal echocardiogram results do not strongly support this diagnosis. The ECG findings and elevated inflammatory markers also support this diagnosis.

rejected.why: Normal coronary arteries make acute coronary syndrome less likely
